verified.body: Issued by {entity} (SEBI reg {reg}). Published {date} via {channel}. Tamper-evident log entry #{seq}.

verified_notice.title: ⚠️ Verified — with notice
verified_notice.body: Validly signed by {entity} on {date}, but the signing key was revoked on {revoked_date}. Confirm on the entity's official channel before acting.

official_claim_unverified.title: ⚠️ Caution — cannot be confirmed
official_claim_unverified.body: This claims to be from {claimed}, but no registered communication matches. Treat it as unsafe.

likely_fake.title: 🚨 High risk — likely fake
likely_fake.body: {top_reason}. Do not act on it. Never pay or share OTPs based on this message.

informational.title: ℹ️ No official claim detected
informational.body: This doesn't claim to be an official market communication. Stay alert for guaranteed-return promises.

advice.sebi_check: Before paying anyone, verify the payee on SEBI Check.

verified.title: Yes, this is genuine
verified.body: {entity} really did publish this. We matched it against their own official record, so you are looking at the real thing.

verified_notice.title: Genuine, but check before you act
verified_notice.body: {entity} did publish this. Since then the digital key used to sign it was reported stolen, so confirm on their official app or website before acting on it.

official_claim_unverified.title: We cannot confirm this
official_claim_unverified.body: This says it comes from {claimed}, but nothing they have officially published matches it. Treat it as unsafe until you check with them directly.

likely_fake.title: This looks like a scam
likely_fake.body: {top_reason} Do not pay anyone, and do not share any code or password because of this message.

informational.title: Nothing official here
informational.body: This does not claim to come from any registered company or regulator. Nothing to verify. Stay alert for anyone promising guaranteed profits.

reasons.SIG_CHAIN_VALID: It carries a valid digital signature from the company.
reasons.C2PA_VALID: It carries valid built-in content credentials.
reasons.C2PA_MISSING: It had no built-in content credentials, which is normal for a forwarded file.
reasons.C2PA_INVALID: Its built-in content credentials did not check out.
reasons.TAMPERED_SIGNATURE: Its digital signature does not check out.
reasons.TAMPERED_CONTENT: It points at a specific official notice, but the content does not match that notice.
reasons.KEY_REVOKED_AFTER_SIGNING: The signing key was reported stolen after this was published.
reasons.HASH_EXACT_MATCH: It is exactly the file the company published.
reasons.PHASH_MATCH: It is the same picture the company published.
reasons.PDQ_MATCH: It is the same picture the company published.
reasons.SIMHASH_MATCH: It is the same message the company published.
reasons.VIDEO_MATCH: It is the same video the company published.
reasons.PHASH_NEAR: It looks close to something official, but not close enough. It may be an edited copy.
reasons.COMM_WITHDRAWN: The company has since withdrawn this notice.
reasons.ENTITY_CLAIM_STRONG: It names a real registered company.
reasons.ENTITY_CLAIM_WEAK: It uses official sounding language without naming anyone.
reasons.HOMOGLYPH_ENTITY: The company name is spelled with look-alike letters to imitate the real one.
reasons.LOOKALIKE_DOMAIN: The web address is a near copy of a real company's address.
reasons.DOMAIN_REGISTERED: The web address really does belong to the company named.
reasons.DOMAIN_NOT_REGISTERED: The web address does not belong to any registered company.
reasons.DKIM_ALIGN_PASS: The email really was sent by the domain it claims.
reasons.DKIM_ALIGN_FAIL: The email was not sent by the domain it claims.
reasons.AUTH_HEADERS_UNAVAILABLE: This was forwarded, so the original email proof no longer travels with it.
reasons.BLACKLIST_MATCH: It matches a scam campaign already being tracked.
reasons.RISK_PHRASES: It uses language common in investment scams.
reasons.PAYMENT_ASK: It asks you to send money directly.
reasons.NO_OFFICIAL_CLAIM: It does not claim to be from anyone official.

why.label: Why this answer

rules.SIGNATURE_VALID: It carries a valid digital signature from a registered issuer, and that signature still checks out.
rules.SIGNATURE_VALID_KEY_REVOKED: The signature was valid when it was made, but the key behind it has since been reported stolen, so we downgrade it rather than call it clean.
rules.REGISTRY_MATCH: We found this exact content in the record of what registered issuers have published.
rules.REGISTRY_MATCH_KEY_REVOKED: The content matches a real publication, but that issuer's signing key has since been reported stolen, so we downgrade it rather than call it clean.
rules.MATCHED_WITHDRAWN: This matches something an issuer published and then withdrew, so it should not be acted on.
rules.CLAIM_WITH_FRAUD_SIGNALS: It presents itself as official and carries active fraud signals. Either alone would be a warning; together we call it a scam.
rules.CLAIM_WITHOUT_MATCH: It presents itself as official, but nothing any registered issuer published matches it. We found no fraud signals either, so we say we cannot confirm it rather than calling it fake.
rules.FRAUD_SIGNALS_NO_CLAIM: It does not claim to be official, but it carries fraud signals we treat as serious on their own.
rules.NO_CLAIM: It does not present itself as an official market communication and shows no fraud signals, so there is nothing to confirm or deny.

why.strict_note: We are deliberately strict: any one of these is enough to call something a scam. We are never strict the other way — failing to find a match only ever means "cannot confirm", never "fake".

stages.signature: Looking for an official digital signature
stages.registry: Comparing it with everything issuers have published

details.reading_video: Video opened, frames sampled and fingerprinted
details.reading_pdf: Document opened and its wording fingerprinted
details.reading_eml: Email opened, sender and links read
details.signature_none: No signature travelled with this file. Forwarding strips it, which is why the next step matters.
details.signature_invalid: A signature was present but did not check out
details.registry_match: Matched something an issuer really published
details.registry_near: Found something similar, but not close enough to call a match
details.registry_none: Nothing an issuer has published matches this

evidence.title: How this was matched
evidence.sha_identical: Byte-for-byte identical to the published file.
evidence.sha_differs: Completely different. Re-encoding rewrites every byte, so exact hashing alone would have missed this.
evidence.fingerprint_video: Compared frame by frame rather than as a single image.
evidence.fingerprint_none: No perceptual fingerprint was compared for this input.
evidence.scale_match: At or below {threshold} differing bits means the same content survived re-encoding, so this counts as a match.
evidence.scale_near: Close, but past the {threshold}-bit match line. Treated as a possible altered copy, not a match.
evidence.scale_miss: Well past the {threshold}-bit match line, so this is not the published content.
evidence.frames_summary: {matched} of {total} sampled frames matched ({percent}%). {threshold}% is the bar for a video match.

image.explain_match: Apps like WhatsApp re-save a photo when you forward it. That rewrites the file completely, but it does not change what the picture looks like. We compare what it looks like, which is why a forwarded copy still checks out.
image.explain_near: This looks close to something official, but not close enough to call it the same. An edited copy of a real notice would look exactly like this, so we do not call it verified.
image.explain_miss: We compared it against every picture issuers have published. The closest one still looks clearly different, so this is not one of theirs.

text.explain_match: Forwarded messages pick up extra spaces, emoji and invisible characters, and those change the message character by character. We compare the wording itself, so a message that has been passed along still matches what the company sent.
text.explain_near: The wording is close to an official message but not close enough to call it the same. Scammers often copy a real notice and change the amount, the deadline or the link, which is exactly what this looks like.
text.explain_miss: We compared this wording against every message issuers have published. None of them says this, so it did not come from them.

document.explain_match: Re-saving or re-printing a document changes the file itself, so we read the words inside it and compare those instead. The wording here matches what the company filed.
document.explain_near: The wording is close to a real filing but not the same. Altering a figure in a genuine document produces exactly this result, so we do not call it verified.
document.explain_miss: We read the words inside and compared them against every document issuers have filed. Nothing they have filed says this.

video.explain_match: Sharing a video re-compresses it, which rewrites the whole file. We take still frames from across the video and compare each one, so a re-shared copy still matches.
video.explain_near: Some frames line up with an official video, but not enough of them to call it the same recording.
video.explain_miss: We took frames from across this video and compared them against every video issuers have published. None of them match.

reasons.SIG_CHAIN_VALID: Digital signature chain is valid and the signing key was active at the time.
reasons.C2PA_VALID: Content credentials (C2PA) manifest is present and valid.
reasons.C2PA_MISSING: No content credentials manifest was found.
reasons.C2PA_INVALID: Content credentials manifest is present but failed to validate.
reasons.TAMPERED_SIGNATURE: The signature does not validate against an active key at the time of signing.
reasons.TAMPERED_CONTENT: This references a specific communication, but the content doesn't match it.
reasons.KEY_REVOKED_AFTER_SIGNING: The signing key was revoked after this content was signed.
reasons.HASH_EXACT_MATCH: Content is byte-identical to a registered communication.
reasons.PHASH_MATCH: Content matches a registered communication's image.
reasons.PDQ_MATCH: Content matches a registered communication's image (PDQ).
reasons.SIMHASH_MATCH: Content matches a registered communication's text.
reasons.VIDEO_MATCH: Content matches a registered communication's video.
reasons.PHASH_NEAR: Content is visually close to a registered communication but not an exact match — possible tampered copy.
reasons.COMM_WITHDRAWN: The matching communication was withdrawn by its issuer.
reasons.ENTITY_CLAIM_STRONG: This content names a specific registered entity.
reasons.ENTITY_CLAIM_WEAK: This content uses official-sounding language without naming a specific entity.
reasons.HOMOGLYPH_ENTITY: The entity name uses look-alike characters to imitate a registered name.
reasons.LOOKALIKE_DOMAIN: This domain closely imitates a registered domain.
reasons.DOMAIN_REGISTERED: This domain is registered to the named entity.
reasons.DOMAIN_NOT_REGISTERED: This domain is not registered to any known entity.
reasons.DKIM_ALIGN_PASS: Email authentication (DKIM) aligns with the sending domain.
reasons.DKIM_ALIGN_FAIL: Email authentication (DKIM) does not align with the sending domain.
reasons.AUTH_HEADERS_UNAVAILABLE: Original authentication headers unavailable on forwarded mail.
reasons.BLACKLIST_MATCH: This matches a known scam pattern.
reasons.RISK_PHRASES: Contains language commonly used in investment scams.
reasons.PAYMENT_ASK: Asks for a direct payment or transfer.
reasons.NO_OFFICIAL_CLAIM: Does not claim to be from any registered entity.
